# A target is a platform and a language, so a declaration may be overridden on
# either axis. The platform's wins where both apply -- the platform has the
# last word on the rest of the build too -- and the declaration's own body is
# what a target neither overrides gets.

# The platform override, on a build whose language is overridden too.
sngl generate --platform html --lang go -o out_hg app.sngl
grep 'html x' out_hg/server.go
! grep 'go x' out_hg/server.go

# The language override, on a platform that has none.
sngl generate --platform fyne --lang go -o out_fg app.sngl
grep 'go x' out_fg/model.go
! grep 'default x' out_fg/model.go

# Neither: the declaration's own body.
sngl generate --platform android --lang kotlin -o out_ak app.sngl
grep 'default x' out_ak/MainScreen.kt

# Two implementations for one target are two answers to a question with one,
# on either axis.
! sngl check dup_language.sngl
stderr 'already has an implementation for "go"'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"
import "sngl:language/go"

component Badge(value string) ui {
    text(value="default " + value)
}

component Badge[go.language] {
    text(value="go " + value)
}

component Badge[html.platform] {
    html.span(textContent="html " + value)
}

component main ui {
    window #w(title="t") {
        Badge(value="x")
    }
}

-- dup_language.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:language/go"

component Badge(value string) ui {
    text(value=value)
}

component Badge[go.language] {
    text(value="a" + value)
}

component Badge[go.language] {
    text(value="b" + value)
}

component main ui {
    window #w(title="t") {
        Badge(value="x")
    }
}
